items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: you could see John Kirby with a band

ctx.x: I heard that band every night that they were up there. And it was a band that had its own way of playing. It was an original, and I'd never heard this kind of music before. Didn't want to sit in, I just wanted to sit and listen to it every night.

And really appreciated what they did as a band. New York at that time, you could hear various sounds. You could walk down 52nd Street and see Barney Bigard playing with a small group at the Onyx. Across the street you could see Billie Holiday, you could see John Kirby with a band, Red -- I mean, Hot Lips Page. Everybody had their own little thing, Coleman Hawkins. There was no copying, like. And Jimmy Ryans and Dixieland, with Jack Teagarden or George Brunis or that sort of sound, what they called Dixieland.…

But each distinct and each mixing and each meeting at the corner bar, or the White Rose and we called it -- the One Rose and we called it the White Rose or the One Rose. And we all -- because you could get that double for ten cents more. A shot was 30, a double was 40.
